lesson.title: Procedure 411 – VERIFICATION OF UNFOUNDED ADDRESSES
objectives: Apply Procedure 411 when a unit cannot locate an incident at the transmitted location.
Verify unfounded addresses by contacting the original source and using callback verification.
Apply Steps 2a–2d for crime-in-progress/major-incident calls when callback fails and/or location is unfounded.
Apply Transit Six-Wire verification steps when the source is the Transit Authority.

questions.stem: Procedure 411: When is this procedure applied?

choices.text: When a supervisor arrives on scene
When a summons is issued
When a field unit cannot find the incident at the location transmitted
When a unit requests a meal break

questions.solution: The SCOPE states it applies when the unit cannot locate the incident at the transmitted location.
questions.hints: Focus on 'cannot find the incident at the location transmitted'.

questions.stem: Procedure 411 Step 1: If the address appears correct but the incident cannot be located, what must the dispatcher do?

choices.text: Wait for a second unit before doing anything
Contact the original source of the event and verify the address
Tell the unit to leave without documenting
Immediately close the job as unfounded

questions.solution: Step 1 requires contacting the original source to verify the address.
questions.hints: You’re verifying the address, not accepting 'unfounded' immediately.
